newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower, pressured by CBOT.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower, pressured by CBOT.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower, with late selling largely in sympathy with the late break in CBOT soft red winter wheat, traders said.

Additional selling near the close appeared to be traders liquidating positions ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday and December's first notice day Friday. Traders expect none to light first day deliveries because the wheat will be needed to load vessels scheduled in Duluth, traders said.
The MGE reported as of Nov. 22, 7.171 million bushels were registered for delivery versus 10.101 million a year ago.
Flour mills were featured early buyers of March with ADM and Peavey each buying 500,000 bushels, traders said.
Spread trade was active early and appeared to involve December positions to March. The spread traded from 29-1/2 to 33 cents premium the December, and closed at 33.5.
In observance of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday Thursday, trading closed at 1210 CST and the exchange will be closed Thursday.
Spring wheat closed down 1-3/4 to up two cents with December up 1-1/4 at $4.24-1/2 per bushel.
MGE December barley futures were lightly traded and closed down one at $6.75 per cwt.
